To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the QMugs dataset provides a large collection of quantum mechanical molecular properties, including wave function matrices, for drug like molecules and (ii) QMugs facilitates the development of machine learning models that predict physical molecular properties on quantum mechanical levels of theory.
we have collected, organized, and published a comprehensive dataset of quantum mechanical properties of a large number of drug like molecules.
we provide an open access dataset of quantum mechanical properties for more than 665,000 drug like molecules, totaling over 2 million conformers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of machine learning techniques for quantum chemistry.
the application of quantum mechanical methods in the context of machine learning and the development of data-driven quantum mechanical force fields.
the development of data-driven approaches in quantum chemistry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QMugs dataset provides the community with a valuable resource to develop and benchmark models that learn from quantum mechanical molecular descriptors.

QMugs provides a large, open access, curated dataset that is intended for the development of machine learning approaches in the field of computational medicinal and chemical sciences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QMugs dataset is the largest open access collection of quantum mechanical properties of drug like molecules.
QMugs is the first open access dataset of its kind and size.
we have created a curated dataset of 665,000 molecules from ChEMBL, which has been optimized at the GFN2-xTB level and has DFT data available.

we have made a large collection of quantum mechanical data available that can be used as a training set in the development of models for quantum chemistry.
